assertions: The sick man will die of this sickness; he will not recover
His disease is a melancholic, cold-and-dry (earthy) affection: fixed-sign, Saturn-ruled obstruction/melancholy humour settled in the body, of long and fixed course rather than a hot acute fever

Death significators converge: the Ascendant is corporally afflicted by a planet part-lord of the eighth, the Sun (temporal light) stands in perfect opposition to Saturn, lord of the sixth, in fixed signs, and the Moon is afflicted in the Ascendant near the Dragon's Tail
method: Horary astrology after Lilly, Christian Astrology Book II sickness judgments: Ascendant and its lord, lord of the sixth, Sun and Moon afflictions, eighth-house testimony
reasoning: All testimony is taken from the positions stated in the figure's prose (no positions invented; the corrupt ascending glyph is not asserted). Death side: (1) Ascendant afflicted by the corporal presence of a planet partly lord of the eighth — the house of life itself invaded by a death significator; (2) sixth house sign fixed and afflicted, its lord Saturn in a fixed, earthly, melancholy sign — the disease is Saturnine: cold, dry, melancholic, fixed and chronic in kind; (3) the Sun, temporal light and chief significator of vitality, in perfect opposition to Saturn, lord of the sixth, in fixed signs — vitality directly opposed by the disease lord with no reception or applying benefic relief stated; (4) Moon, significator of the body and its humours, near the Dragon's Tail (Cauda) and afflicted in the Ascendant — bodily strength corrupted at the Ascendant itself. No counter-testimony (strong lord of Ascendant, benefic assistance, Moon separating to benefics) is present in the stated positions, so the judgment is death, not recovery. Disease identification follows the sixth-lord's sign quality: fixed + earthly + melancholy = black choler/melancholy humour, obstruction of a fixed and lingering kind. Timing scale: fixed signs and Saturn argue weeks-to-months rather than days; the window is therefore set in weeks with the focal crisis as the single main coordinate (the double-layer rule applied to this event question); no exact day is claimed, since the stated positions support a focal week, not a day.
summary: The patient will die; his disease is a fixed melancholic (cold, dry, earthy) affection.
timing: Window: a fixed-sign, Saturnine course — the crisis runs on a scale of weeks within the fixed-sign period following 16 July 1645 (fixed signs give a slow, drawn-out measure, not days); main coordinate within the window: the completion of the Sun–Saturn opposition's separation, i.e. the crisis point in the weeks immediately after the figure date, assigned to late July–August 1645 as the single main coordinate range's focal week (first full week of August 1645)
